subject: geography
chapter_title: The Origin and Evolution of the Earth

concepts.title: Early Theories: Nebular Hypothesis to Big Bang
concepts.definition: Early theories of the earth's origin include the nebular hypothesis of Kant and Laplace with a slowly spinning cloud of gas, tidal theories of a passing star, and the modern Big Bang theory of a singular huge explosion about 13.7 billion years ago expanding the universe from the size of a point.
concepts.key_idea: The Big Bang expanded space, formed hydrogen and helium gases, and gravity condensed matter into galaxies and stars, with the solar system forming about 4.6 billion years ago.

concepts.title: Evolution of the Earth: Planets, Moon and Life
concepts.definition: The solar system evolved from a disc shaped cloud of gas and dust with planetesimals accreting into planets; the moon formed by the giant impact or big splat theory, and the earth's evolution shows differentiation of layers, loss of primordial atmosphere and development of the present atmosphere and oceans enabling life.
concepts.key_idea: The evolution of life began in the oceans about 3.8 billion years ago with single celled blue green algae, long before the oxygen rich atmosphere formed.

concepts.title: The Solar System, Planets and the Earth as a Unique Planet
concepts.definition: The solar system holds eight planets of which Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are terrestrial rocky planets while Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are jovian gas giants, and the earth alone sustains life because of its ideal distance from the sun, water, atmosphere and ozone shield.
concepts.key_idea: The earth's size and distance from the sun hold gases and water in the right balance, which is why it is called a privileged or unique planet.
